Patcham Junior School
Be curious, not judgemental
Welcome to Patcham Junior School
It is a privilege and pleasure to welcome you to Patcham Junior School.
Patcham Junior School is a warm, inclusive and ambitious school community where children are encouraged to develop a love of learning, believe in themselves and achieve their very best. At the heart of our school is our vision:
"Be curious, not judgemental."
These four words capture so much of what we value. We encourage children to approach the world with curiosity, to ask questions, explore ideas and embrace new challenges. At the same time, we teach them to be kind, respectful and open-minded, celebrating that every person in our school is unique and valued.
Whether you are already part of our school community or considering Patcham Junior School for your child, I hope our website gives you a flavour of the values, opportunities and experiences that make our school unique.
I look forward to welcoming you to our school and working together in the years ahead.
Georgie MannersHeadteacher

Families
“Patcham Junior School is a lovely school which promotes warmth, community spirit and most importantly every child’s individuality, through allowing children to feel safe and express themselves; giving them pride and confidence.”
“I cannot think of any way to improve the school!”
” I feel (my child) has had many great opportunities and has made great progress through being inspired. Thanks to all.”
Quotes from parent feedback, July 2016.
We believe that it is vital to form strong and positive relationships with the parents and carers of the pupils attending our school. We set out to do this in a number of ways, but primary through operating an ‘open door’ system. This means, at the end of the day, families always have the opportunity to pop in to talk to a teacher if they have any questions or concerns. If parents want a longer meeting, or an opportunity to discuss something at length, it always helps to book an appointment with us because we do have many meetings and tasks before and after school and we don’t like to offend! Families can contact the school office to arrange a meeting with any member of staff.
Families are able to attend formal consultation evenings with their child’s teacher in the autumn and spring terms and receive a full report in the summer. Newsletters are sent home regularly and a dedicated parents association organises school events to raise funds. There are also plenty of opportunities throughout the year to attend concerts, performances, sports occasions and so on. We are also bursting with parents who help in classrooms and around school on anything and everything. We feel that this truly captures the sense that our school is a community within a community. Their help is welcomed and the staff appreciates it greatly.
We are very keen on working with parents to improve our school. This year, following feedback, we have:
Implemented a range of new parent workshops, open afternoons and opportunities for parents to discuss key decisions
Included all new entrants in the buddy writing project
Improved our website and made information easier to find
Increased the amount of communication, for example more newsletters.
You have the right to expect the best service from us. We will try to provide that service with respect and dignity. In return we ask the same from all of our parents and carers. Further information can be found here:

Music
Music forms an important element in the creative arts curriculum of the school. Our music policy ensures that every child in the school experiences a wide variety of musical activities.
Class music is taught by a specialist music teacher. We use a wide range of instruments and have a music room, which is used for class and instrumental lessons. The music skills we aim to develop include singing, listening and appraising, composing and performing. Children also learn about music from various historical eras as well as music of different cultures and countries of the world. All children have the opportunity to learn the ukulele - each child will complete a ukulele topic each year and will develop their skills as they move up the school. We have ukuleles at school but children are welcome to bring in their own ukuleles for these lessons.
We have a whole school singing assembly each week and we weave singing into many aspects of the school day.

Patcham Junior School
Governors
Governors’ Role
The governors’ role is to oversee the strategy of the school; to act as a sounding board for issues being reviewed within the school and to ensure that the school is accountable to all stakeholders including parents, staff, pupils, Brighton and Hove Local Authority and the local community. Governors are not involved in the day to day running of the school, which is managed by the Senior Leadership Team. The Department for Education (DfE) has a guide for governors: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/governance-in-maintained-schools and all agree to act according to the PJS Governors Code of Conduct 2025.
The full governing body usually meets three times a term. Its functions include but are not limited to ensuring:
Structure of the Governing Body
The legal structure allows for: 3 elected parent governors, 1 local authority governor, 1 elected staff governor, 1 headteacher staff governor and 9 co-opted governors. The staff governor is elected from and by the staffing body and parent governors are elected from and by the parent body. The local authority governor is appointed by the governing body and approved by the local authority. With the exception of the headteacher governor, all governors are appointed for a term of 4 years, may resign at any time and are not automatically reappointed at the end of their term. The Headteacher may choose to be a headteacher governor. The full governing body may also appoint associate members on the basis of their skills, to support them in their work. They do not have a vote. All appointments by the governing body are entirely guided by the skills and experience offered by the individuals in order to make the governance of the school effective. Diversity is important and we collect diversity data from its members. It is confidential but is regularly analysed and used in recruitment and training.
Decisions are mostly made by the full governing body apart from those taken by the Pay and Staffing Committee, with terms of reference here. Powers have not been delegated to individual governors.
The governing body is lead by co-chairs of governors - Louise McCusker and Richard Enticknapp.
They may be contacted via the school office or by email - louisemccusker@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk or richardenticknapp@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk
Click here to find out who is in the governing body at Patcham Junior School. To read the minutes of meetings click here.
Vacancies
There are currently vacancies in the co-opted governor category. We would be interested to hear from potential volunteers who have an interest in school improvement and have skills and experience in any of: Finance, Education, Business, Health and Safety, Strategic Planning, reflect the diversity of or have links in the Patcham community.
Governors are all volunteers who wish to make a positive contribution to the school and the education of all its students and governors find it a rewarding experience. The governing body’s overriding responsibility is to work in partnership with the Headteacher, to promote the continuous improvement in the performance of the school. We play an important part in raising school standards through our three key roles.
We take training seriously and there is a full induction programme for new governors and excellent training provided by the local authority to ensure we maintain the skills necessary to fulfil our role.
If you are interested in joining or assisting the governing body, please contact either co chair of governors: louisemccusker@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk or richardenticknapp@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk for further information and an application form is here. Further information is also available from:
http://www.brighton-hove.gov.uk/content/children-and-education/schools/school-governors
Becoming a School Governor in Brighton and Hove
What am I letting myself in for?In serving as a governor, you would need to commit to attending three evening meetings per term, take time to attend governor training courses and get to know the school, including working with school staff to understand the school’s plans and activities by visiting the school, perhaps once per term. In time you would be expected to develop an area of specialism and contribute to working groups as required from time to time as appropriate.
Contacting the Governors
If you wish to contact the governors, you can either email the school office via the form on our contact page, email either of the co-chairs, louisemccusker@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk or richardenticknapp@patchamjun.brighton-hove.sch.uk or write to:
Chair of Governors, Patcham Junior School, Ladies Mile Road, Brighton, BN1 8TA

I have several management qualifications, including a Masters Degree in Public Service Management.’
Current term of office expires 17.3.2030. Marion was originally appointed as local authority governor 1.3.2011.
I am a retired ex Careers Adviser and teacher. I moved to Brighton just under 5 years ago and have found lots to keep me busy in retirement. I have always maintained a connection with young people and schools, even when living in America, where I made the costumes for the local High School Musical!
Term of office 7.12.23 to 6.12.27 (original term commenced 10.12.19)
I am excited to join the governing body as a parent governor and to contribute to the school and help develop it where I can. I have a daughter who is in Year 4 and am also an ex-pupil myself. I currently work at another secondary school in Brighton as an HR & Admin manager and have worked in educational settings since 2012 so appreciate the pressures they face and deal with on a daily basis. I also co-ordinate the event 'Let's Dance' at Brighton Dome which involves schools and groups from all over the city which has helped me create good relationships with other schools and see over 20,000 students take part in the years I have been involved. I am passionate about providing students with opportunities to learn and develop outside the classroom and am heavily involved with the Duke of Edinburgh Award - offering this to students in the school that I work in and also as a freelance assessor to other schools across the region. I am hoping my experience and knowledge will add to the already strong governing body and am excited to be involved further in the school community.
Clerk to the Governors
My main function is to support the governing body as its administrator, information manager and governance professional. I do not have a vote. I also provide advice in and outside meetings to ensure the governing body works in accordance with the legal framework and uses its time well to benefit pupils in the school. I am proud to work with such a dedicated team of volunteers and school staff.

Welcome to Patcham Juniors Noticeboard!
Patcham Junior School

Patcham Junior School
Noticeboard - FOPJS Events
Dear Families and Carers,
It feels impossible that we are already heading towards the final weeks of the school year! We have an action-packed couple of months ahead, and we are very excited about all the events coming up. Please see the poster for full details.
Thank you so much for all your support in the spring term. The Easter Egg Hunt feels like a long time ago now, but we really appreciated everyone who came along and got involved in saying farewell to Mr Sutherland.
A really huge thank you also goes to the brilliant band Padre, who so kindly gave up their afternoon to keep us entertained and rocking out.
As you have probably guessed, the whole of FOPJS and the school team were absolutely delighted with the progress made at Dig Day. It really showed just how much can be achieved when there is a big group of willing helpers. We hope to see more of this kind of community spirit over the coming years — you truly can make a difference to your children’s time at school, and Dig Day was proof of that.
Please don’t forget our Coins to Change campaign. If you have any foreign coins or notes from any country, you can bring them in and drop them into the donation pot by the office. This is such a simple way to raise money for the school, but it will make a great difference and be a real benefit to our children.
We tried very hard to arrange a final disco this term but were unable to find a suitable date with our action-packed months ahead.
There is still plenty for the children to look forward to, particularly the High School Musical production, which pupils and staff are working so hard to prepare for.
Year 6 Leavers’ DiscoThis is not a PTA-led event, so it will be down to Year 6 parents and carers to organise and run it. Some financial support will be available from FOPJS, but the event will only be able to go ahead if volunteers come forward to help organise it.If you are able to help, please contact the school office or email friendsofpatchamjuniors@gmail.com
Sponsored Read FundraiserOur final big fundraiser of the year will be our Sponsored Read. We are excited to get the children involved in celebrating reading while raising money for the school.We know this time of year can feel very busy, so participation is flexible. Families can donate online or take part using sponsor forms.We are raising money for AR Reader — a hugely valuable resource that supports reading across the school and helps foster confidence, progress, and a love of books in our children.Sponsor forms will be available to print off next week, and our JustGiving page goes live on Thursday.
Thank you, as always, for all your continued support this year. We are looking forward to finishing the summer term in style!
